A_8_1.title: User Endpoint Devices
A_8_1.description: Laptops, phones and other user devices are set up and managed so that the information on them is protected, for example with encryption, screen lock and remote wipe.

A_8_2.title: Privileged Access Rights
A_8_2.description: Administrator and other far-reaching rights are restricted and managed, and their use is controlled. Recommendation: as few people as possible, only for as long as needed.

A_8_3.title: Information Access Restriction
A_8_3.description: Access to information and to system functions is limited according to the access rules.

A_8_4.title: Access to Source Code
A_8_4.description: Read and write access to source code and development tools is limited to the people who need it.

A_8_5.title: Secure Authentication
A_8_5.description: Logins use methods that fit the risk, so that the person logging in is the person they claim to be. Recommendation: multi-factor authentication for remote access and administrator accounts.

A_8_6.title: Capacity Management
A_8_6.description: The company watches how much computing power, storage and network it uses and plans ahead so that systems do not run out.

A_8_7.title: Protection Against Malware
A_8_7.description: Devices and systems are protected against malware, and staff know how to spot it. Recommendation: endpoint protection, email filtering and limited rights to install software.

A_8_8.title: Management of Technical Vulnerabilities
A_8_8.description: The company learns about vulnerabilities in the systems it uses, assesses how exposed it is, and fixes or mitigates them in time.

A_8_9.title: Configuration Management
A_8_9.description: Secure settings for hardware, software, services and networks are defined, applied and kept under control.

A_8_10.title: Information Deletion
A_8_10.description: Information that is no longer needed is deleted from systems, devices and storage media, in line with legal and contractual retention rules.

A_8_11.title: Data Masking
A_8_11.description: Where data does not need to be seen in full, it is masked, pseudonymised or anonymised, for example in test systems or reports.

A_8_12.title: Data Leakage Prevention
A_8_12.description: Measures stop sensitive information from leaving the company unnoticed, by email, upload, storage media or other channels.

A_8_13.title: Information Backup
A_8_13.description: Copies of information, software and systems are made regularly, and restoring them is tested.

A_8_14.title: Redundancy of Information Processing Facilities
A_8_14.description: Systems that must stay available have enough redundancy, such as a second server or line, to keep running when one part fails.

A_8_15.title: Logging
A_8_15.description: Systems record relevant activities, errors and security events, and the logs are protected and kept for a set time.

A_8_16.title: Monitoring Activities
A_8_16.description: Networks, systems and applications are watched for unusual behaviour so that possible incidents are noticed and acted on.

A_8_17.title: Clock Synchronization
A_8_17.description: The clocks of all systems are synchronised, so that logs can be compared. Recommendation: one reliable time source for all of them.

A_8_18.title: Use of Privileged Utility Programs
A_8_18.description: Tools that can get around system or application controls are limited to the few people who need them, and their use is controlled.

A_8_19.title: Installation of Software on Operational Systems
A_8_19.description: Software is installed on production systems only through a controlled process, by authorised people.

A_8_20.title: Networks Security
A_8_20.description: Networks and network devices are secured and managed so that the information passing through them is protected.

A_8_21.title: Security of Network Services
A_8_21.description: The security features and service levels of network services, in-house or bought in, are defined and checked.

A_8_22.title: Segregation of Networks
A_8_22.description: The network is divided into separate zones, for example office, servers, guests and production, so that a problem in one zone does not spread.

A_8_23.title: Web Filtering
A_8_23.description: Access to websites is filtered to keep staff away from harmful content.

A_8_24.title: Use of Cryptography
A_8_24.description: Rules say where and how encryption is used, which methods are allowed and how keys are managed.

A_8_25.title: Secure Development Life Cycle
A_8_25.description: Security rules apply throughout the development of software and systems, from requirements to release.

A_8_26.title: Application Security Requirements
A_8_26.description: Security requirements are set before applications are developed or bought.

A_8_27.title: Secure System Architecture and Engineering Principles
A_8_27.description: Principles for designing secure systems are written down and applied in every development and change.

A_8_28.title: Secure Coding
A_8_28.description: Developers follow secure coding practices to avoid common weaknesses. Recommendation: work from a public reference list such as the OWASP Top 10.

A_8_29.title: Security Testing in Development and Acceptance
A_8_29.description: Security is tested during development and before new or changed systems are accepted.

A_8_30.title: Outsourced Development
A_8_30.description: When development is outsourced, the company sets the security requirements and checks that they are met.

A_8_31.title: Separation of Development, Test and Production Environments
A_8_31.description: Development, test and production run in separate environments, so that work in progress cannot affect live systems.

A_8_32.title: Change Management
A_8_32.description: Changes to systems and IT facilities follow a controlled process. Recommendation: each change is requested, assessed, approved, tested and recorded.

A_8_33.title: Test Information
A_8_33.description: Data used for testing is chosen and protected with care, and production data is used in tests only with protection that matches it.

A_8_34.title: Protection of Information Systems During Audit Testing
A_8_34.description: Audits and technical tests on live systems are planned and agreed with the system owners, so that they do not disrupt operations.
